extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order excluding a registered practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 based on reciprocal discipline (state disbarment), setting out the grounds, required notices, account prohibitions, and reinstatement framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order I: 'Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.' The Final Order applies to preparing/filing documents and practicing before the Office until reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline is predicated upon violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice states the exclusion is 'predicated upon being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.' Reciprocal discipline under §11.24 may be imposed where a practitioner has been disbarred by a state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and consequence of no response (40‑day deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice was delivered and signed; Respondent did not file a response. The Analysis states that because Respondent failed to file a response, 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)' and reciprocal exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: electronic FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 2 requires electronic publication for public review; disciplinary decisions are available at the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Exclusion' text describing the respondent, registration number, and basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 3 includes sample Notice of Exclusion text (name, registration number, summary of state disbarment findings and violated rules) to be used in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline, and the reasons for the discipline, to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 4 directs dissemination of discipline information consistent with §11.59 to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 5 requires compliance with §11.58 duties (not restated in the document) — practitioners should consult §11.58 for specific post-discipline obligations (e.g., client notification, file transfer, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authority to disable or suspend USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent as of the date of the Final Order (including all accounts Respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with any matter before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 6 grants OED/USPTO authority to disable/suspend accounts to prevent further practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining USPTO verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 7 bars the practitioner from seeking or being added to verified electronic accounts until reinstatement under §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using or assisting others to use USPTO filing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is prohibited from using, accessing, or assisting others in using or accessing any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 8 prevents circumvention by using another's account or assisting others to access USPTO systems on Respondent's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific enumerated prohibitions until reinstatement per 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition for reinstatement is granted pursuant to §11.60, Respondent shall be prohibited (and the USPTO is authorized to disallow) from: (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) for preparing/filing documents; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for any such accounts; (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials in connection with USPTO.gov accounts; and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov accounts for preparing/filing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 9 lists four discrete prohibited acts to prevent indirect access to USPTO electronic filing capabilities while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: No USPTO obligation to reactivate disabled/suspended accounts; respondent's responsibility for re‑activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the order obligates the USPTO to take action sua sponte to re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended; it is Respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order 10 clarifies that reactivation is not automatic and must be initiated by the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct findings supporting state disbarment (failure to obey court order and maintain respect)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found Respondent culpable for failing to obey a court order and to maintain respect due to the courts, by failing to timely advance fees to court‑appointed discovery referees and failing to timely pay two sanctions orders, in violation of California Business and Professions Code §§ 6103 and 6068(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice summarizes these findings as supporting the Supreme Court of California's disbarment order; such failures to obey court orders and to pay advance fees/sanctions are grounds for state discipline and thus for reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct finding: failure to report a judgment against him (breach of fiduciary duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found Respondent failed to report a judgment against him in favor of his prior patent clients, dated May 8, 2015, for breach of fiduciary duty, in violation of Business and Professions Code § 6068(o)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to report adverse judgments relating to professional conduct can be an independent disciplinary violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct finding: seeking to mislead a judge / act of moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found Respondent sought to mislead a judge by knowingly making a false and misleading statement to a court in claiming not to have been served with the prior sanctions order, constituting an act of moral turpitude in violation of Business and Professions Code §§ 6068(d) and 6106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing misrepresentation to a tribunal (moral turpitude) is an aggravated basis for disciplinary action and supports disbarment/reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct finding: failure to update state bar membership address (obfuscation)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found Respondent failed to update his membership address after moving his office, thereby obfuscating his location, in violation of Business and Professions Code § 6068(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to keep bar contact information current can hinder disciplinary processes and is a punishable violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of intentional misconduct and evasion of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar Court found Respondent's misconduct was intentional: he 'evaded the civil discovery process with purpose, in a course of "unacceptable gamesmanship," and lied to the superior court about not having been served with an order for sanctions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionality and deliberate evasion/lying are aggravating factors that support harsher discipline and are relied upon in the reciprocal discipline determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites federal statutory/regulatory authority as the basis for imposing reciprocal discipline; practitioners should consult these authorities for procedural and substantive rules governing practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification requirements for Final Order (mailing addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent's most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a) and to any address where the OED Director reasonably believes Respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate of Service documents the mailing to two addresses (most recent membership address and where OED reasonably believes respondent receives mail); proper service is a procedural prerequisite to finalizing discipline.
